ActionItem.description:
One thing a student could do next, worked out from their marked answers.

Only comprehension and missed questions give rise to one. Engagement never
does: how someone's camera or click rate read says nothing about what they
should study.

and whether anyone has seen it.

session. The three figures at the end are those of a topic difficulty alert,
null for any other kind.

Authenticate a user and return a bearer token.

Development uses the fixed Cyber 1 development identities.
Production resolves users through Nour's persisted User table.

get.description: Return the authenticated user's identity and consent state.

post.description:
Swap a still-valid access token for a fresh one.

The client calls this shortly before its token expires, so a class longer
than the token's lifetime is not interrupted by a sign-in. The account is
checked again, and the sign-in itself still ends max_sign_in_hours after
the password was typed. An expired token cannot be refreshed: the user
signs in again.

until a different admin approves the request and it is executed.

Carry out an approved request. Deleting a session removes everything it
holds and cannot be undone. Erasing a student deletes their own data and
anonymises their account.

The summaries kept for a student after their session data was deleted.

Purge every session past the retention period, and the Teams roster
syncs past it. Cannot be undone, so the body must say `"confirm": true`.
Audited with the counts.

Returns 202 immediately after the uploaded file passes security validation.
Processing then runs in the background and reports progress over the
WebSocket as `material.progress` events.

get.description:
The review queue for a material.

Lecturer/admin only, same as the mutation routes --
QuestionOut carries correct_option, which must never reach a student or
a lecturer who didn't upload this material. A lecturer sees only their
own; an admin sees everything.

Approve, edit or reject a generated question. No question reaches a
student without passing through here.

Replace a draft question with a newly generated one from the same page.

The draft is rejected rather than deleted and the replacement is returned
as a new draft. Refused with 409 for a question that is not a draft, and
503 when the generator is unavailable or returns nothing usable.
Backs the 'approve all' and 'stage N questions' actions.

200.description: One JSON object per line, each with `type` and `request_id`. `accepted` comes first. Then either `delta` events carrying `text`, `citation` events carrying a `citation` (`id`, `material_title`, `source_page`, `source_slide`, `excerpt`), `follow_up` events carrying a `prompt`, and `completed`; or one of `unsupported` (with a `reason`), `empty_retrieval` and `error` (with a `detail`).

One student's results for one session: what they attempted and missed,

and comprehension are separate fields and never combined.

A student reads only their own; staff read those of a session they run
(and leave an audit trace when it is not their own). A session, a student
or a pairing the caller may not see are all the same 404.
